name: Country
who: The national government: the President, Parliament (National Assembly and Senate) and the courts.
note: Passports, visas, police, the national ID card and income tax all sit at this level.

name: County
who: Elects a governor and a county assembly. Each county also sends a senator and a woman representative to Parliament.
note: Created by the 2010 constitution, with the first county governments in 2013. Counties run local health, roads, markets, parking and business permits.

name: Sub-county
who: A national-government administrative unit, headed by a deputy county commissioner. Below it come locations and sub-locations, run by chiefs and assistant chiefs.
note: It often has the same name and boundary as a constituency, which is why people mix the two up.
verify: The number of national-government sub-counties changes as new ones are gazetted; confirm the current total and that Westlands sub-county matches Westlands constituency.

name: Constituency
who: Elects one MP to the National Assembly. Boundaries are drawn by the IEBC (the electoral commission).
note: When someone says “my MP”, this is the area they mean.

name: Ward
who: Elects one MCA (Member of the County Assembly), who represents the ward in the county government.
note: Wards are the smallest unit you vote in. Their names often join two neighbourhoods with a slash.
verify: Confirm Parklands/Highridge is still one of the wards of Westlands constituency after the latest IEBC boundary review.

name: Estate or neighbourhood
who: No official status at all. This is what people actually say when you ask where they live.
note: “Estate” can mean a gated housing scheme or a whole neighbourhood. Its edges are fuzzy, and it may not match any ward.
